findings.title: OAuth token exchange request not validated/logged on failure
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, safe_urlopen response is not checked for HTTP status before parsing; if GitHub returns an error page/body, parse_qsl silently produces an empty dict and the code falls into generic error() without any logging of the failure reason (e.g., invalid_grant, rate limiting). This makes debugging GitHub-side failures (expired code, revoked app, API outages) difficult and could mask abuse attempts (e.g., repeated invalid code use) since there's no logging/metrics around failed exchanges.

findings.title: github_authenticated_user validation only triggers when Integration already exists
findings.body: The check comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] only runs when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` succeeds (i.e., integration already created by webhook) and OrganizationIntegration does not yet exist. If the Integration record does not exist yet at this point in the pipeline (e.g., webhook delivery is delayed/race), the code returns pipeline.next_step() at the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch without ever validating github_authenticated_user, bypassing the newly added security check. This creates a race condition where a malicious actor could complete installation before the webhook-created Integration record propagates, bypassing user validation entirely.

findings.title: No validation that get_user_info succeeded with a 200 response
findings.body: get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) is called without checking that the underlying request succeeded (e.g. GitHub API outage, rate limiting, or revoked token could cause errors). If get_user_info raises an exception (e.g., ApiError) this is not caught here, so an unhandled exception could propagate and produce a 500 error instead of the intended user-facing error page, which is inconsistent with the rest of the flow's error handling pattern reflected elsewhere in this method (try/except around token parsing).

findings.title: installation_id bound to pipeline state in OAuthLoginView redirects to GitHub before validating organization context
findings.body: self.determine_active_organization(request) is called, but if the user is not authenticated or has no valid organization, nothing prevents proceeding to the OAuth redirect; this doesn't match prior behavior where organization context was established before any installation steps. This may be intentional but is not covered by tests validating unauthenticated/invalid org access during this new OAuth hop.
